result.summary: Allows running txindex on pruned nodes as long as the index database contains no legacy file-offset entries. When looking up a transaction located in a pruned block, txindex, RPC, and REST endpoints return the candidate block hashes so callers can retrieve the block using getblockfrompeer. It also allows an already-pruned node to build a partial index starting from its earliest unpruned block, exposing the starting height via getindexinfo.

evidence: PR description: 'After #35531, each txindex entry now points to the block hash containing the tx instead of the file location of the block... This PR enables maintaining a txindex while pruned.'
Removes the long-standing initialization error 'Prune mode is incompatible with -txindex' in src/init.cpp.
result.card: Allows Bitcoin Core nodes to run txindex concurrently with block pruning. When a queried transaction resides in a block that was pruned after being indexed, RPC and REST lookups return the block hash rather than a generic miss, enabling the caller to retrieve it on demand with getblockfrompeer. An already-pruned node can also initialize a partial txindex starting from its oldest retained block, tracking and reporting the start height in getindexinfo. This removes the long-standing restriction that prevented storage-constrained pruned nodes from indexing transactions.
